title: Solving the Rational Inequality x/2 > 1 + 4/x Graphically and Algebraically
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: (a) Compare the graphs of f(x) = x/2 and g(x) = 1 + 4/x to identify the values of x for which x/2 > 1 + 4/x. (b) Confirm the solution set algebraically.

steps.title: Interpret the Inequality Geometrically and Rearrange to Zero
steps.explanation: Geometrically, x/2 > 1 + 4/x holds where the line y = x/2 lies strictly above the hyperbola y = 1 + 4/x. Algebraically, subtract 1 + 4/x from both sides so that we can analyze the sign of a single rational expression.
steps.why: We must avoid multiplying both sides by x directly because x can be either positive or negative.

steps.title: Combine Over a Common Denominator and Factor
steps.explanation: Put all terms over the common denominator 2x to get (x^2 - 2x - 8)/(2x) > 0, and factor the quadratic numerator as (x - 4)(x + 2).
steps.why: Factoring the numerator and denominator exposes all critical points where the rational expression can change sign: x = -2, x = 0, and x = 4.

steps.title: Perform Sign Analysis on the Four Test Intervals
steps.explanation: Test the sign of (x - 4)(x + 2)/(2x) on (-inf, -2), (-2, 0), (0, 4), and (4, inf): on (-inf, -2) it is (-)(-)/(-) = -; on (-2, 0) it is (-)(+)/(-) = +; on (0, 4) it is (-)(+)/(+) = -; and on (4, inf) it is (+)(+)/(+) = +. Thus the inequality holds on (-2, 0) U (4, inf).
steps.why: Each simple linear factor changes sign at its root, causing the rational expression to alternate signs across (-2, 0, 4).
